invariants.name: invalid events are rejected, never normalized

invariants.description: each record hash is SHA-256 over the canonical event map merged with prev_hash; the first record of the ledger links to GENESIS_HASH; record N links to N-1 iff prev_hash equals record N-1's hash AND seq equals record N-1's seq plus 1; any mismatch surfaces as a named failure: bad_record_hash, broken_link, or sequence_gap
invariants.name: the hash chain commits to content and order

invariants.description: one append-only JSONL file per shard (shard-NNNNNN.jsonl, zero-padded index); append continues the verified head — seq derived from the head record and prev_hash from the head hash or the previous shard's root — and never rewrites existing shard content; line-level parse errors report the shard and line number
invariants.name: the shard store is append-only

invariants.description: the Merkle root is pairwise SHA-256 over the shard's record hashes with an odd final leaf duplicated; the Ed25519 signature covers the canonical JSON of {count, kind: seal, merkle_root, prev_shard_root, sealed_at_ms} — signature and public_key are not part of the message; flipping any seal field breaks the signature, and a count mismatch is bad_seal_count
invariants.name: seals commit to the Merkle root and record count

invariants.description: compact_last_sealed replaces the last sealed shard with a single compaction record carrying the original seal verbatim and keeping the shard's genesis prev_hash, so root links into and out of the shard are unchanged; the new seal (count 1) re-signs over the compaction record; rewriting a compacted shard breaks the seal signature; the original content is no longer reconstructible from the ledger
invariants.name: compaction preserves the cross-shard root link

invariants.description: at verify time every ledger event is evaluated against every policy rule: a deny rule flags any event matching its set matchers, a require_outcome rule flags a matching event whose decision outcome differs; violations appear as policy_violation failures carrying the rule_id
invariants.name: policy evaluation is per-event and per-rule

invariants.description: verify exits 0 clean, 1 tampered (bad_record_hash, broken_link, bad_merkle_root, broken_root_link), 2 gap (sequence_gap), 3 signature (bad_signature, bad_seal_count), 4 policy (policy_violation), 5 corrupt (parse_line, invalid_event, bad_seal_structure), 255 usage; when several classes coexist the most specific diagnosis wins in the order corrupt, gap, signature, tampered, policy
invariants.name: exit codes form the CI contract with fixed precedence

invariants.description: export emits one JSON document with deterministic typed shard serialization (never the raw stored lines, so file key order cannot leak); importing an exported ledger's events (without seq — it is derived) into a fresh ledger reproduces identical record hashes
invariants.name: export and import round-trips are hash-stable

invariants.description: given an uncorrupted copy of the sealed shards and a known public key, verify proves content integrity, ordering and completeness within a shard, seal integrity, cross-shard continuity, and the compaction boundary; it does not prove: total replacement by a private-key holder with a re-signed shard, unanchored pre-seal history, shard loss (detected, not repaired), the truthfulness of written events, or membership of the policy file in the signed boundary
invariants.name: the threat model states exactly what verify proves

invariants.description: for every u32 shard index up to 999_999 the store name shard-NNNNNN.jsonl round-trips back to the exact index through the directory-scan parser, has fixed width 19, and lexicographic name order equals numeric index order (which is what makes the store's sorted scan sound)

invariants.description: record N links to record N-1 iff prev_hash equals record N-1's hash AND seq is the exact u64 successor of record N-1's seq; the successor is never taken modulo the u64 ceiling — no seq may link past u64::MAX (the chain cannot wrap) — and on the guarded domain (prev below u64::MAX) the predicate is exactly seq == prev + 1
